cl_mix_opioid_tolerance_loss.q: Why can the usual amount be dangerous after a break?
cl_mix_opioid_tolerance_loss.short: Because tolerance may drop during a break, reviews say. In one study, 3 people died of an overdose after a hospital detox. All 3 had stayed for the whole programme.
cl_mix_opioid_tolerance_loss.but: Nobody measured anyone's tolerance. And it's 3 deaths in one small study.
how: 137 people were followed for a year after a 28-day hospital detox in London. All 3 overdose deaths came within 4 months, among the 37 who finished both the detox and the programme. None of the 100 who left earlier died that way.

The researchers read this as lost tolerance but never measured it. The people who died also differed in other ways: 4 of the 5 who died from any cause had lived alone, against 16 in 100 of the others.
Two reviews offer the same idea but give no numbers: not how long a break must be, how fast tolerance falls, or how much the risk rises. The main study behind them looked at hair samples.
One review describes two studies of people on methadone. Their tolerance to its effect on breathing was not complete.
cl_mix_opioid_tolerance_loss.rate: One small study after a hospital detox: 3 overdose deaths, and nobody measured tolerance. Plus two reviews, one citing the other, with no numbers.

cl_opi_conditioned_tolerance.q: Can using in a new place make an overdose more likely?
cl_opi_conditioned_tolerance.short: Maybe. In rats, heroin was more often deadly in a new place. In people, nobody has tested it well. One study asked 10 overdose survivors what was different.
cl_opi_conditioned_tolerance.but: That's 10 people's memories, about 5 years later, with nobody to compare them with. Only 3 of them recalled a new place or crowd.
how: The idea: the place, the people and the ritual that come with a drug start to trigger the body's push-back against it. That push-back is part of tolerance, so it may be weaker somewhere new.
In rat studies from the same researcher, tolerance was weaker in a new place, and a large dose of heroin was more often deadly there. Rats aren't people.
Of 10 overdose survivors, 7 recalled something unusual that day: 3 a new place or crowd, 2 a different way of injecting, 2 a different mix of drugs. The other 3 recalled nothing unusual.
Nobody counted how often people use somewhere new without an overdose. The review suggests a treatment based on the idea, but cites no test of it.
cl_opi_conditioned_tolerance.rate: One tiny study of 10 people's memories, with nobody to compare them with, plus rat experiments from the same researcher. Rat findings don't show what happens in people.

cl_opi_treatment_mortality.q: Is it dangerous to stop methadone or buprenorphine (Suboxone)?
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.short: The weeks after leaving were the riskiest. In 5 studies, deaths in the first 4 weeks off methadone ran at about 32 a year per 1,000 people, against 6 in steady treatment.
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.but: These studies counted everyone who left, for any reason. People who leave differ in other ways, so the studies can't show that stopping itself caused the deaths.
how: In 16 groups of people on methadone, about 11 in 1,000 died each year in treatment, against about 36 out of it. Every group had more deaths out of treatment.
In the biggest recent groups the gap was smaller: about 6 or 7 deaths a year per 1,000 people in treatment, against 12 to 18 out of it.
Deaths in the first 4 weeks off methadone ran at about 32 a year per 1,000 people, against about 14 later on. The first month on methadone looked riskier too, but that could be chance.
Deaths counted as overdoses didn't clearly rise after leaving, in the 3 groups that split them by time. Buprenorphine had just three groups, mostly one Australian study.
cl_opi_treatment_mortality.rate: Sixteen studies in several countries all found more deaths out of treatment than in it. But nobody chose at random who stayed, and people who leave may differ in other ways, so how much is due to stopping is unknown.

cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.q: Can opioid withdrawal itself kill you?
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.short: It has happened, but nobody knows how often. One editorial lists 11 deaths, all in jail. It links them to vomiting and diarrhoea that dried people out and went untreated.
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.but: It's one editorial's list, built from news reports and a court case. With no count of how many people went through withdrawal, there's no rate.
how: The authors' idea: vomiting and diarrhoea that don't stop, left untreated, dry the body out. Blood sodium rises, and the heart can fail.
The cases: a woman in custody in the UK in 1998, and 10 people in US jails reported in the press from 2013 to 2016, aged 18 to 49.
The authors say each death came slowly, with time to treat it, and call the deaths neglect or a lack of medical care.
They say such deaths are rising but give no counts over time. Nothing here covers withdrawal outside custody.
cl_opi_withdrawal_deaths.rate: One editorial, using cases from news reports and a court case, all in custody. Nobody counted how many people went through withdrawal, so how often it kills is unknown.

interactions.statement: People on methadone become fully tolerant to its effect on breathing.
interactions.why: One review describes two studies of people on methadone: their tolerance to its effect on breathing was not complete.

heroin.statement: In one study, people who stayed to the end of a detox programme had fewer overdose deaths later.
heroin.why: The opposite: all 3 overdose deaths came among the 37 who finished it, and none among the 100 who left earlier. The researchers suspect lost tolerance, but nobody measured it.

heroin.statement: In rats, heroin was more often deadly in a new place than in the usual one.
heroin.why: In one researcher's rat studies, yes. In people, it has only been looked at in 10 overdose survivors' memories, with nobody to compare them with.

heroin.statement: Death rates were about the same in and out of methadone treatment.
heroin.why: In 16 groups of people on methadone, about 11 in 1,000 died each year in treatment, against about 36 out of it. People who leave differ in other ways, so this can't show cause.

heroin.statement: You can't die from opioid withdrawal.
heroin.why: Deaths have been reported, all in jail, linked to vomiting and diarrhoea that dried people out and went untreated. How often it happens is unknown: the list comes from one editorial.

general.statement: Big studies of people show a new place makes an overdose more likely.
general.why: In people, there's one study: 10 overdose survivors recalling the day about 5 years later. Only 3 recalled a new place or crowd.

methadone-buprenorphine.statement: The first weeks off methadone were the riskiest time in studies.
methadone-buprenorphine.why: In 5 studies, deaths in the first 4 weeks off methadone ran at about 32 a year per 1,000 people, against 6 in steady treatment. People who leave may differ in other ways.
